The fact that the proposal for the Council is made by so highminded and fair a man as the present High Commissioner loses the weights consideration it might normally have had when we recall that Britain is troubled with Nationalistic itchings in Egypt and India and is forced to make some dramatic gestures to mol lify Arab sentiment. This issue, dark and foreboding as it appears, may carry its compensatory balm if it creates, as it shows every prospect of doing, the much needed united front in Zionist ranks within and without Palestine. By MRS. BERNARD KAUFMAN The question of a legislative council for Palestine is the most immediate and vital one affecting Palestinian Jewry today and represents the first step towards self-government. Shall we accept participation in such a body while we are a minority and while the ratio of Arab to Jew is 800,000 to 350,000? This is the issue we must face. With the disproportion in population, are we prepared to release Great Britain of her obligation under the Mandate and the Balfour Declaration to establish the Jewish National Home, and lay ourselves open to discrimination by a hostile Arab majority? There is grave apprehension among the Jews in Palestine over the involvements that will ensue. Great Britain recognizes these and has inserted safeguards.
